name: Hollywood Burbank/Bob Hope Airport
before:
The Los Angeles airport most people forget about, three miles north west of downtown Burbank. For anything in Hollywood, Glendale, Pasadena or the San Fernando Valley it is a good deal closer than LAX, and closer to Griffith Park, Universal Studios and downtown Los Angeles too.

It is also the only airport in the area with a direct rail link to downtown Los Angeles, served by two stations, Burbank Airport-North and Burbank Airport-South.

Two things to prepare a client for. There are no jet bridges at all, so every boarding is down air stairs onto the apron. And the route map is mostly western United States, with regular flights to Atlanta, Honolulu and Indianapolis and a seasonal New York service, so this is not a substitute for LAX on a long haul itinerary.

Two runways serve the 555 acre site. Aircraft generally take off on Runway 15 into the southerly wind and land across on Runway 8, which is the only one with an instrument landing system and clear ground on the approach.
after:
A Los Angeles area airport, three miles north west of downtown Burbank and about 12 miles from downtown Los Angeles. It is closer than LAX to many of the region's popular attractions and serves Hollywood, Glendale, Pasadena and the San Fernando Valley.

Metrolink trains link it directly to downtown Los Angeles, running to Union Station from two stations, Burbank Airport-North and Burbank Airport-South.

Two things to prepare a client for. There are no jet bridges, so boarding is at ground level. Most routes are to the western United States. Those further afield include Atlanta, Honolulu, Indianapolis and, in season, New York, so this is not a substitute for LAX on a long haul itinerary.

Two runways serve the 555 acre site. Aircraft generally take off on Runway 15 and land on Runway 8.
